query: In this study, we analyzed several possible types of homing gene drives for population suppression of the malaria vector Anopheles gambiae. Various parameter sets for each of these drives were considered, representing alternative explanations for fertility measurements previously conducted (Simoni et al., 2020; Kyrou et al., 2018; Hammond et al., 2021). We found that the drive that combined a homing drive and X-shredder may actually be less capable of suppressing a population than the original dsx drive with the zpg promoter alone, particularly in a spatially continuous population.
matched_segment: In this study, we analyzed several possible types of homing gene drives for population suppression of the malaria vector Anopheles gambiae. Various parameter sets for each of these drives were considered, representing alternative explanations for fertility measurements previously conducted (Simoni et al., 2020; Kyrou et al., 2018; Hammond et al., 2021). We found that the drive that combined a homing drive and X-shredder may actually be less capable of suppressing a population than the original dsx drive with the zpg promoter alone, particularly in a spatially continuous population.
